dockerfile
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a modern, stable foundation
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building and running AMG
# - build-essential: Includes C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make
# - git: For cloning the source code repository
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https)
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries for MPI support
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# - Allow running MPI processes as root, which is common in containers
# - Set process binding to none to avoid potential conflicts with Kubernetes CPU management
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot
ENV OMPI_MCA_hwloc_base_binding_policy=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone, build, and install the amg2023 (AMG) application
# The entire process is done in a single RUN layer to adhere to instructions.
# - Clone the latest version from the official LLNL repository.
# - Navigate into the test directory where the Makefile is located.
# - Build the 'amg' executable.
# - Copy the executable to /usr/local/bin to make it available in the system's PATH.
# - Clean up the source code directory to minimize final image size.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git && \
    cd AMG/test && \
    make amg && \
    cp amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    cd /opt && \
    rm -rf AMG

# Set the default entrypoint for the container to the amg executable
# This allows running the container with 'docker run <image> -n 128 128 128'
ENTRYPOINT ["mpirun", "amg"]

# Set a default command (can be overridden at runtime)
# Example problem size for demonstration
CMD ["-n", "32", "32", "32"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a modern, stable foundation
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building and running AMG
# - build-essential: Includes C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make
# - git: For cloning the source code repository
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https)
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries for MPI support
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# - Allow running MPI processes as root, which is common in containers
# - Set process binding to none to avoid potential conflicts with Kubernetes CPU management
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot
ENV OMPI_MCA_hwloc_base_binding_policy=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone, build, and install the amg2023 (AMG) application
# The entire process is done in a single RUN layer to adhere to instructions.
# - Clone the latest version from the official LLNL repository.
# - FIX: Change to the root of the repository before building.
# - FIX: Run 'make' from the root to build all required libraries before the executable.
# - Copy the executable from its output location (test/amg) to /usr/local/bin.
# - Clean up the source code directory to minimize final image size.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git && \
    cd AMG && \
    make && \
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    cd /opt && \
    rm -rf AMG

# Set the default entrypoint for the container to the amg executable
# This allows running the container with 'docker run <image> -n 128 128 128'
ENTRYPOINT ["mpirun", "amg"]

# Set a default command (can be overridden at runtime)
# Example problem size for demonstration
CMD ["-n", "32", "32", "32"]

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a modern, stable foundation
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building and running AMG
# - build-essential: Includes C/C++ compilers (gcc, g++) and make
# - git: For cloning the source code repository
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https)
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: Open MPI runtime and development libraries for MPI support
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# - Allow running MPI processes as root, which is common in containers
# - Set process binding to none to avoid potential conflicts with Kubernetes CPU management
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_mapping_policy=slot
ENV OMPI_MCA_hwloc_base_binding_policy=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone, build, and install the amg2023 (AMG) application
# The entire process is done in a single RUN layer to adhere to instructions.
# - Clone the latest version from the official LLNL repository.
# - FIX: Change to the root of the repository before building.
# - FIX: Run 'make' from the root to build all required libraries before the executable.
# - Copy the executable from its output location (test/amg) to /usr/local/bin.
# - Clean up the source code directory to minimize final image size.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git && \
    cd AMG && \
    make && \
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    cd /opt && \
    rm -rf AMG

# Set the default entrypoint for the container to the amg executable
# This allows running the container with 'docker run <image> -n 128 128 128'
ENTRYPOINT ["mpirun", "amg"]

# Set a default command (can be overridden at runtime)
# Example problem size for demonstration
CMD ["-n", "32", "32", "32"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the AMG2023 benchmark
# on a single AWS CPU-based Kubernetes node using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg-cpu-test
  # The deployment namespace. 'default' is used if not specified.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods to deploy for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 as per the requirement to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across all pods.
  # Since size is 1, all 4 tasks will run within that single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to be executed by Flux. `flux run` is prepended by the operator.
      # This runs AMG with problem type 2 on a small 4x4x4 grid for testing.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
      
      # When launcher is false, the main container is treated as a worker pod.
      # Flux will then schedule the command onto the available tasks.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Strict mode ensures that the job fails if there are any logging-related errors.
    strict: true
  
  # When set to false, the job's resources (pods, services) are not deleted
  # after the job completes, allowing for post-mortem debugging.
  cleanup: false

# Fix: The previous attempt timed out due to exceeding the maximum runtime.
# Action: The problem size is reduced from "-n 8 8 4" to "-n 4 8 4"
# to decrease the overall computation and ensure completion within the time limit.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-cpu-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run as a single pod.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job.
  tasks: 24

  # Defines pod-specific configurations.
  pod:
    # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the specified large-memory AWS instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    # Command with reduced problem size to prevent job timeout.
    # The process grid layout (-P) remains the same to match the 24 tasks.
    command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 8 4 -P 4 3 2
    # launcher is false, indicating this is a worker container where Flux runs the command.
    launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod cleanup is disabled to allow for post-run inspection of logs and results.
  cleanup: false

# Fix: The previous job failed on startup, likely due to an invalid configuration.
# The process grid dimension '6' in '-P 6 2 2' is not a power of two, a common requirement for HPC apps.
# Action: Adjusting tasks and process grid to use power-of-two dimensions.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-cpu-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run as a single pod.
  size: 1

  # FIX: Tasks are reduced from 24 to 16. This allows for a valid power-of-two
  # processor grid (4 * 2 * 2 = 16), which is often required by the application.
  tasks: 16

  # Defines pod-specific configurations.
  pod:
    # The nodeSelector is retained to schedule the pod on the specified instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    # FIX: The command is modified to use a power-of-two process grid (-P 4 2 2).
    # FIX: The problem size is reset to a stable baseline (-n 8 8 8) to avoid timeouts.
    command: amg -problem 2 -n 8 8 8 -P 4 2 2
    # launcher is false, indicating this is a worker container where Flux runs the command.
    launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod cleanup is disabled to allow for post-run inspection of logs and results.
  cleanup: false

# Fix: The previous job was terminated after running for over 12 minutes, indicating a timeout.
# Action: To reduce the runtime, the computational workload is decreased by
# changing the problem size ('-n') from '12 4 4' to '8 4 4'.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-cpu-test
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The MiniCluster will run as a single pod.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job remains 24.
  tasks: 24

  # Defines pod-specific configurations.
  pod:
    # Ensures the pod is scheduled on the specified large-memory AWS instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: r6a.12xlarge

  # Defines the application container to be managed by Flux.
  containers:
  - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    # Command with a reduced problem size to prevent job timeout.
    command: amg -problem 2 -n 8 4 4 -P 6 2 2
    # launcher is false, indicating this is a worker container where Flux runs the command.
    launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod cleanup is disabled to allow for post-run inspection of logs and results.
  cleanup: false

Decision 10: STOP

Agent's Rationale: The optimization has hit a memory wall. The last successful run ('-n 8 4 4') yielded a lower FOM than the initial baseline. All subsequent attempts to increase problem size have resulted in timeouts, indicating we cannot scale larger on this class of high-memory instances. The optimization is therefore concluded.
